newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Powerful earthquake rocks Indonesia's Java island.
newsitem.headline: Powerful earthquake rocks Indonesia's Java island.

text.p: An earthquake measuring 6.0 on the Richter scale rocked the Indonesian capital Jakarta on Monday afternoon, sending people scurrying out of high-rise buildings.
Officials at the meteorological department said the earthquake was centred below the sea-bed in the Indian Ocean, some 300 km (200 miles) southwest of Jakarta.
There were no immediate reports of damage or casualties.
Police in the town of Pelabuhan Ratu, on the southwest coast of Java island, said there were no reports of damage or tidal waves.
Tall buildings in Jakarta shook when the tremor hit the city at about 3:10 p.m. (0810 GMT) and people rushed out onto the street.
Traders fled the stock exchange, brokers said, but returned after about half an hour. The exchange was not officially closed despite the panic.
"There were lots of traffic jams in the business district because all the people in those tall office buildings came out on the street," said one witness.
"Things were really swaying out here," said a guest staying in an upper floor of the Mandarin Oriental Hotel. He said people rushed out of the building but there was no damage.
The Indonesian archipelago is regularly hit by earthquakes.
